title: Mates are natural in the non-adjoint sides of the square
statement:
Let $L_1\dashv R_1$ ($L_1:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, counit $\varepsilon_1$) and $L_2\dashv R_2$ ($L_2:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, unit $\eta_2$) be adjunctions, $G,G':\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $H,H':\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ functors, $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ a natural transformation with mate $\alpha^\flat:GR_1\to R_2H$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and $\sigma:G'\to G$, $\tau:H\to H'$ natural transformations. Then the mate of $(\tau L_1)\circ\alpha\circ(L_2\sigma):L_2G'\to H'L_1$ is
$$
 (R_2\tau)\circ\alpha^\flat\circ(\sigma R_1):G'R_1\to GR_1\to R_2H\to R_2H'.
$$
(Proof sketch for the splitter: in the component formula of the mate, move $\sigma$ past $\eta_2$ by naturality of $\eta_2$ and $\tau$ past $\varepsilon_1$ by naturality of $\tau$.)
